summary: Prince George's County, MD 100-foot tower completed 1931 near Hillmeade; a railroad fire was reported from it that year; FFLA lists it gone.

facts.status_note: Forest Lookout Association's Maryland list marks it gone; no source read says when or how it came down or what remains

staffing.status: lookout-watchman E. O. Brown in charge of the observatory in 1931; later staffing not in the sources read

events.note: Anne Arundel County contributed $400 toward a lookout tower planned near Hillmeade
100-foot tower recently completed at Hillmeade, reported July 1931
Lookout-watchman E. O. Brown in charge of the Hillmeade observatory
Small fire started by the Pennsylvania Railroad at Tuxedo, 8 miles from the tower, reported by Brown; put out by smokechaser Daniel B. Wiseman before it burned 1/8 acre

evidence.supports: Anne Arundel County contributed $400 toward a lookout tower planned near Hillmeade in 1930
evidence.quote: During 1930, the county contributed $400 towards a lookout tower, which is to be erected in 1931, near Hillmeade, Prince Georges County.

evidence.supports: a state report said the planned tower would provide detection for a very important forest area in Anne Arundel County
evidence.quote: The proposed tower will provide detection for a very important forest area in Anne Arundel County.

evidence.supports: July 16, 1931 newspaper reported the 100-foot tower recently completed
evidence.quote: A tower 100-foot high was recently completed at Hillmeade, Prince George's County.

evidence.supports: November 6, 1931: lookout-watchman E. O. Brown in charge of the Hillmeade observatory and reported a fire started by the Pennsylvania Railroad at Tuxedo
evidence.quote: Lookout-watchman E. O. Brown, in charge of the Hillmeade observatory, reported a small fire started by the Pennsylvania Railroad at Tuxedo

evidence.supports: the Tuxedo fire was eight miles from the tower
evidence.quote: This fire was 8 miles from the tower.

evidence.supports: fire put out by smokechaser Daniel B. Wiseman before it burned 1/8 acre
evidence.quote: which was extinguished by Smokechaser Daniel B. Wiseman before it had burned 1/8 acre

evidence.supports: Forest Lookout Association lists the Hillmeade tower as gone
a map site still lists a Hillmeade Lookout Tower near Fairwood
evidence.quote: Hillmeade Lookout Tower is situated nearby to the village Fairwood

notes_for_editor: Brief height 30.5 m matches the 100-foot figure in the 1931 newspaper. Brief staffing 'unknown' replaced with the 1931 lookout-watchman. Only 1930-31 newspaper items, the FFLA 'gone' status and a map label were found; two web searches (the second found no removal record) and about two page reads. No removal date or site description found. Mapcarta is an automatically generated map page, cited only for its label, not as evidence that a structure stands. The 1931 fire narrative names the railroad as the starter; the sources do not say how the fire was classed.
